test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Breathing is harder at high altitudes compared to the sea level because _____.

options.text: the concentration of oxygen is very high at high altitudes
the atmosphere is less dense at high altitudes
the rate of diffusion of gases is decreased at high altitudes

solution:
The correct answer is__** the atmosphere is less dense at high altitudes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Breathing is harder at high altitudes** compared to sea level
 
• It is **because the atmosphere is less dense at high altitudes.**
 
• This means that **the air is thinner, and there is less oxygen available for the body to breathe in**
 
• There is a **decrease in atmospheric pressure as well as the oxygen content of the atmosphere resulting in a lower partial** pressure of oxygen than that of carbon dioxide resulting in difficulty in breathing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Altitude Sickness

 
 
• At sea level, there are around 21% more oxygen molecules than usual.
 
• While the concentration does not change with the increase in altitude but the amount of oxygen molecules per breath and the atmospheric pressure decreases.
 
• At 12,000 feet (3,658 metres), there are around 40% less oxygen molecules in each breath.
 
• Even while at rest, your breathing rate needs to increase for the body to receive enough oxygen.
 
• Continued exposure to higher altitudes without enough acclimatisation might result in very serious, even fatal illnesses.
